title: LG32-381: full leaf tables and 32-input merges listed by Grover, Q = O(2^((17/25) sqrt n)), S_C = S_Q = O(2^((1/4) sqrt n)), T = O(2^((381/100) sqrt n))

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single LG32-381 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 2^28; otherwise r0 = ceil(sqrt n), w = floor(499 r0/2000), y32 = ceil(1358 r0/10000), Hb = ceil(3129 r0/1000), a collimation tree of 32 binary levels and then y32 32-input levels with measured windows, with leaf tables built directly from about w qubits and listed by fixed-length Grover runs over hashed blocks of all-pairs guesses with lists in qubits, with tables of at most about 2^w entries, the free-frequency odd-part decoder and the controlled-shift 2-adic part) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(2^((381/100) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is T = O(n^14 2^(3.808 sqrt n)). The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^((381/100) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the classical-memory, quantum-memory and sample bounds of the other claims.

For the same LG32-381 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak classical memory on every execution branch is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((1/4) sqrt n)) bits, with an absolute constant, including depth-first merge tables, classical evaluation of the listing circuit, the lists Tl and decoder records. The stronger main-branch bound is S_C = O(n^2 2^(0.2495 sqrt n)). The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((1/4) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, quantum-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LG32-381 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^((1/4) sqrt n)) qubits, with an absolute constant, including the depth-first index registers, the qubits holding guess-dependent lists during Grover search and all ancillas. The stronger main-branch bound is S_Q = O(n^3 2^(0.2495 sqrt n)). The envelope B_Q(n) = 2^((1/4) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LG32-381 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, is O(2^((17/25) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is Q <= n Ccap + K = O(n^3 2^(0.679 sqrt n)), with Ccap and K defined in proof.md. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((17/25) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work and memory bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LG32-381 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
